"Generate a comprehensive game design document and foundational code structure for a multiplayer open-world survival and creature-collecting game.
​Core Concept: The player explores a sprawling open world, surviving against environmental hazards, hostile factions, and capturing wild creatures that are utilized for combat, base building, and automated resource farming.
​Creature Mechanics: Creatures possess distinct elemental affinities, active combat skills, and specific utility traits (e.g., watering, mining, crafting, kindling). Players capture them using a projectile-based trapping mechanic that calculates success based on creature health, status effects, and trap tier.
​Player Combat @COMMENT_BODY@ Survival: The player character manages stamina, health, and hunger. Combat blends third-person shooter mechanics (crafting and using firearms, bows, and rocket launchers) with melee attacks, allowing the player to fight concurrently alongside their deployed creatures.
​Base Building @COMMENT_BODY@ Crafting: A modular building system where players construct shelters, assembly lines, and farms. Captured creatures can be assigned to the base to automate crafting queues, generate power, and gather resources based on their specific utility traits.
​World @COMMENT_BODY@ Progression: The map features distinct biomes (forests, deserts, volcanic regions, and snow peaks) with dynamic weather. Progression relies on a technology tree unlocked through leveling up, allowing players to build advanced machinery and better weapons.
​Art Style: Stylized, vibrant 3D graphics with anime-inspired creature designs contrasting with realistic modern weaponry and survival gear.
​Output the core gameplay loop, a breakdown of the primary data structures needed for the creature and crafting systems, and a starter C# script for the projectile-based creature capture mechanic. (3D Game, Phone/Tablet)

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
18: 
19: ## Mobile browser games
20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
24: - Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

Read file start.sh, lines 1-4
1: #!/usr/bin/env bash
2: set -euo pipefail
3: cd "$(dirname "$0")"
4: /usr/bin/time -p node "${RUNTIME_DIR:?}/scripts/default-start.mjs"

The repository is essentially a blank canvas, so I’m building this as a self-contained, mobile-friendly browser game rather than assuming a Unity project exists. I’ll include the playable prototype, a game design document, and a Unity-ready capture mechanic/data foundation.
